passages.note: Third-reading Yea on a single-subject joint resolution; 40 of 97 voting members were Nay, so the near-unanimous rule does not apply.

passages.provision_quote: Only a marriage between one (1) man and one (1) woman shall be valid or recognized as a marriage in Indiana.
passages.note: Engrossed House text prints the whole operative addition in one sentence; nothing inside a [deleted: …] fence is relied on.
Official bill page records his co-authorship and gives the first name (Matthew Lehman) that the surname-only roll call lacks.
passages.actor_quote: Co-Authored by: Rep. Timothy Wesco, Rep. Wes Culver, Rep. Rhonda Rhoads, Rep. Robert Heaton, Rep. Don Lehe, Rep. Matthew Lehman, Rep. Randall Frye.

rows.reasoning: Lehman co-authored HJR 3 (2014) and voted Yea on its third reading, a single-subject constitutional amendment whose entire operative addition reads "Only a marriage between one (1) man and one (1) woman shall be valid or recognized as a marriage in Indiana." That text both defines marriage as only between one man and one woman and denies validity or recognition to any same-sex marriage, matching the rung "Make same-sex marriage illegal and define marriage as only between one man and one woman." It recognizes no civil unions, so the rung allowing "civil unions for same-sex couples, but reserve marriage for opposite-sex couples" is excluded.
